Dear Mr. Dorrell and Selection Committee, MECO Engineering Company, Inc. (MECO) is pleased to present qualifications to the City of Kirksville, MO for professional engineering services related to Water Treatment Plant Improvements.

MECO Engineering is celebrating its 40th anniversary this year. This long-spanning history has been built on serving municipalities, such as yours, in a vast span of projects with varying needs, requirements, funding, and challenges. We take pride in gaining the majority of our business from repeat, satisfied customers. MECO currently has seven office locations, with a location conveniently close for all your project needs in Kirksville, MO, mere miles from the project site. This close proximity, as well as our knowledge of the area and ever-changing regulations, allows us to assure you of our ability to serve the City of Kirksville, MO in a high-quality, cost-effective manner.

MECO specializes in civil engineering, specifically water/wastewater projects. We have tackled various sizes, scopes, and challenges through our years of experience specifically in water treatment plants. We are also currently handling a $66 million project that includes water treatment, wells, and coordination with several different government entities. We can assure you we are the perfect choice for your project on grounds of current experience, long-term experience, and convenience. In planting an office location in Kirksville, MO, we have proven our investment in the community and would be honored to be chosen to continue to serve in this capacity in which we are uniquely qualified.
MECO has the honor of serving as the engineering consultant for many water projects. Some of these include:

This long-spanning success of serving communities has given us experience in projects spanning multiple disciplines and unique challenges. MECO also keeps up to date with state and federal regulatory agencies to assure we are able to serve our clients with the most current standards and practices. *A few of MECO’s most relevant projects are included in this submittal.

MECO currently has 60 professionals with many talents and continue to welcome more team members to our dedicated team as we expand. Our firm is well-positioned and highly qualified to be considered as your consultant and engineer for this selection process based on expertise, knowledge, and experience.
Max Middendorf, PE, Water Engineering Expert
Kevin W. Garnett, PE, Civil Engineer

Based in part on the feedback we gained meeting with Kirksville’s key water department personnel, and getting a tour and review of the City of Kirksville Water Treatment Facility, MECO can provide both short term and long term strategies to meet the city’s water demands. We recognize the condition of the current facility and have strategic cost effective solutions to maximize the equipment lifespan. We have Lidar 3d scanning technologies that make rehabbing existing treatment facilities a faster and more cost effective solution. In addition to strategic planning, we have the local presence to ensure all standard operating procedures are meeting all regulations and operating with standardized procedures. Our office is a mere 6 blocks away from the plant allowing MECO to be on site at a moments notice. We have the expertise, experience, and lack of conflict to handle all aspects of your project in house.

MECO’s “Standard of Care” and “Project Approach” is a team-centric based philosophy to ensure that every step of project scope development and design review fully invests the client in each step of the process. MECO does not believe in an engineer-driven project development process; we see the most value in investing our client input in the process, first and foremost. Our clients will never see MECO force a project or a solution upon them. Our clients will always lead the initiative for developing projects and working with our professional staff to determine the best suited solutions to their needs. You can rely on MECO and our Project Team to provide the attention to detail, prompt response, and a level of commitment to service, experience, knowledge, and expertise that you require and expect of your Engineering Consultant. We never forget that clients have many choices and options in their selection process for a consulting engineering firm. We would be honored to be selected to serve the City of Kirksville in this capacity. For questions, or to meet with your project team, please feel free to contact through phone or email at 660-280-2010 or rhuseman@mecoengineering.com. Sincerely yours, MECO Engineering Company, Inc. Set to go to bid in June of 2025 is a newly formed regional water system with Illinois Alluvial Regional Water Company. This is a $210M project serving 7 members with an 8MGD wellfield, 3 miles of 30" raw water transmission main, a new 8 MGD water treatment plant, 2 1 MG clearwells, 2 MG composite elevated water tower and 50 miles of finished water transmission main. $66 million in government funding was applied for and granted for this project
*Images are highly accurate renderings. Project goes to bid June 2025
The City of Pittsfield, IL undertook a major water system improvements project in 2009 to provide a safe and reliable drinking water supply to their community.

Supply In order to meet state and federal standards for drinking water, the city realized the need to replace their existing surface water supply (lake), with a ground water supply provided through a new alluvial well field, including two 1,000 GPM wells (approximately 95-ft), submersible pumps, elevated platforms, piping and electrical.

Treatment The new ground water supply is treated by a new 1,000 GPM Ion-Exchange ground water softening plant. A new SCADA system links all systems and facilities to monitor and control the operations. A diesel-powered emergency backup generator provides emergency service to the two new wells and a diesel-powered generator has capacity to operate the new water treatment plant at full capacity.
Curran-Gardner Township Public Water District Curran Gardner Township, IL

Water System Improvements: $5.6M water system expansion (two 750,000 gallon elevated towers/ one new 300 GPM well/pumping 2 stations/59,700 LF mains); project coordination, planning, consulting. Project also consisted of: 57,000 LF new waterline (owner- constructed), new gen-set backup generator for water treatment plant, new 6,600 SF office and maintenance building. MECO became the Water District’s Engineer in 2002. Since then, Wells #1 and #2 were chemically treated, motor and controls were elevated and the pumps/motors were replaced. Well #5 was also completed at this time with a submersible turbine pump installed to deliver an additional 500 GPM. Well #6 was completed in 2012 to provide an additional 300 GPM to the district for treatment. In 2019 MECO was also hired for a Water Treatment Plant expansion project to add 3 new dual stage filters and 1,000 gpm clarifier, and new chemical feed systems, a new motor control center and SCADA controls.

The scope of services was for the design engineering of the basement area for Louisiana’s Water Treatment Plant to address corrective piping to drains, dripping seals and leaking fittings. To reduce the humidity from the basement, a design to seal off this area will be incorporated with the installation of a HVAC/Remote air handler. The awarded contractor will coordinate the rental of a commercial dehumidifying unit to reduce the moisture and will be paid by the city. Once the moisture has been reduced, then the basement can continue to be addressed with the identified replacement of corroded fasteners and bolts as well as prepping and painting of existing piping. The plans will also include a separate sheet to address the installation of a new door and frame at the pump house as identified / requested by the City of Louisiana. Construction engineering covered the pre-construction meeting as well as progress meetings, the administration paperwork associated with contract documentation and required bonds/insurance as well as any pay application, change orders, and final paperwork. Construction engineering also covered the part-time inspection portion to cover the critical time an inspector needs to be present or follow up on ensuring the work has been completed with inspection reports and photographs.

This project was sped up due to the use of NavVis Lidar 3D scanning technology that MECO has invested in. This scanner collects points from all angles and compiles them to create images accurate to within increments of a millimeter. The bonus feature is it fractions data collection time. Entire buildings can be fully scanned and modeled in less than an hour.

After our meetings with the city to gain further understanding of the project and the plant, MECO is confident in being able to be a one-stop-shop for all of the City of Kirksville's Water Needs. With MECO's breadth of knowledge and extensive bench, we will handle all aspects of your water treatment facility design in-house. From short-term improvements to long-term capacity expansions, we are experts in all scopes of water treatment plant improvements and can give your city the plan it needs to better service the community.

Funding We not only have technical expertise, but we are well versed in helping all available funding sources including USDA, SRF, and CDBG. This is put on display with our current water treatment project that was granted $66 million in federal funding.

Short-Term MECO can develop a plan to ensure the current facility performs to its maximum capacity. We have detailed, tested and proven strategies to fix your nonoperational valves, rebuild service pumps, ensure proper chemical feeds, and preserve your structural piping and supports.

Long-Term For future expansion, MECO staff have the knowledge to develop long-term site expansion and capital planning. We frequently establish long-term plans, and therefore are confident in our abilities to assist the City of Kirksville in developing a proper 2-20 year capital depreciation plans. We understand including preparing proposed site locations, negotiating with land owners, securing contracts for land purchase, and providing proposed water treatment technologies. We are experts in design plants with clarifiers that have no moving parts and provide unprecedented lifespans. MECO is well versed in semi autonomous water treatment, ensuring back up procedures for outage free service.
